title: Detection of the degree of an ordinary fraction at homogeneous primes
statement: Let A be an N-graded commutative ring with grading 𝒜 and let f be homogeneous of positive degree b. Let k be an integer and z an element of the ordinary localized module A_f. Suppose its image in A_p lies in the degree-k part (the fiber used in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]) at every homogeneous prime p in D₊(f). Then z belongs to degreeZeroFractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions] for the shifted grading: it is represented by a homogeneous numerator y of degree k+n and a homogeneous denominator h in powers of f of degree n, with the numerator required to be zero if k+n is negative.

source.place: Lemma 27.8.4 and its preceding construction, specialized to the shift A(k); this split separates ordinary gluing from degree detection

proof.text: Use the existing proved localization_kernel_isHomogeneous from ProjBasicOpenLocalizationDetection [lem-sc-proj-basic-open-localization-detection], brought into proof scope by import all. It states that ker(A → A_p) is homogeneous for every homogeneous prime p. No duplicate polynomial construction or kernel theorem is needed.

Write z=a/s with s=f^r, of degree n=r*b. At each p avoiding f use hz and the definition of the degree part [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. If z maps to zero, homogeneousness of the kernel kills every component of a. Otherwise write its value as u/h with u homogeneous of degree l, h homogeneous of degree j outside p, and l=j+k. Clearing denominators gives h*a−s*u in the homogeneous kernel. Its component of degree j+i is h*a_i when i≠k+n, because s*u has degree n+l≠j+i. Since h is a unit in A_p, a_i maps to zero. This is the fully proved private helper twist_local_component_zero.

Apply basicOpen_localization_detection [lem-sc-proj-basic-open-localization-detection] to the image of each unwanted component a_i and zero in A_f. Step 2 shows their images agree in every A_p on D_+(f), hence every component with i≠k+r*b vanishes in A_f.

Sum the finite homogeneous decomposition using DirectSum.sum_support_decompose. If k+r*b≥0, only its component in degree (k+r*b).toNat survives. Use that component as numerator and the original s=f^r as denominator. Their fraction equals z by IsLocalization.mk'_eq_iff_eq and LocalizedModule.mk_cancel, yielding membership in degreeZeroFractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]. If k+r*b<0, every component vanishes, z=0, and the zero numerator with the same denominator is permitted by the shifted grading. Thus no denominator enlargement, auxiliary Z-graded localization, or Laurent-polynomial construction is needed; nilpotent f and an empty basic open are covered by the existing detection theorem.

proof_origin.place: Tag 01M7, Lemma 27.8.4 and the preceding homogeneous-fraction construction; full Lean proof by K3 reusing the existing private localization_kernel_isHomogeneous via import all and the existing basicOpen_localization_detection. Local shifted-degree separation and finite-sum reconstruction are proved directly. Repair removes the duplicate kernel proof and its polynomial helpers.

lean.statement: theorem twist_degree_detection {A σ : Type v} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A] (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜] (k : ℤ) (f : A) (b : ℕ) (hb : 0 < b) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 b) (z : LocalizedModule.Away f A) (hz : ∀ p : basicOpen 𝒜 f, IsLocalization.map (M := Submonoid.powers f) (T := p.1.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal.primeCompl) (Localization.AtPrime p.1.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal) (RingHom.id A) (Submonoid.powers_le.mpr p.2) z ∈ HomogeneousLocalization.degreePart 𝒜 p.1.asHomogeneousIdeal.toIdeal.primeCompl k) : z ∈ degreeZeroFractions (fun n : ℕ ↦ (𝒜 n : Set A)) (fun n : ℕ ↦ {y : A | if 0 ≤ k + n then y ∈ 𝒜 (k + n).toNat else y = 0}) (Submonoid.powers f)
